successCriteria.description: tests/unit/modules/employee/employee.routes.test.ts no longer casts a partial object to IEmployeeService; the fake passed to the `employeeService` seam is a complete object implementing all five IEmployeeService methods (createEmployee, getEmployeeById, getEmployeeByEmail, getEmployeesByManagerId, getEmployeeProfileById).

The four IEmployeeService methods the route under test does not call (createEmployee, getEmployeeById, getEmployeeByEmail, getEmployeesByManagerId) are throwing stubs, so any accidental invocation fails loudly rather than silently returning undefined.

The existing four GET /employees/me route tests (200 profile, 401 no user, 401 invalid role, 404 no profile) continue to pass unchanged after the fake is expanded, and the suite still typechecks under strict TypeScript with no `as unknown as` / partial-object cast on the service fake.

tests/unit/modules/auth/auth.service.test.ts is verified already compliant (full five-method IEmployeeService fake with throwing stubs, and JWT_SECRET saved before beforeAll and restored in afterAll) and requires no modification in this phase.

constraints: Test-only phase: no production source files (src/) may change. The only file in scope is tests/unit/modules/employee/employee.routes.test.ts.

The fake must satisfy the IEmployeeService interface structurally (no `as unknown as IEmployeeService` or partial-object cast); the five methods are exactly those declared in src/modules/employee/employee.service.interface.ts.
The four unused methods must throw (not return undefined/null or a no-op), matching the throwing-stub pattern already used in tests/unit/modules/auth/auth.service.test.ts.
Do not change the route under test, the `employeeService` decoration seam, the actor-resolution hook, or any existing test assertion — only the shape of the fake service object.
outOfScope: Any change to tests/unit/modules/auth/auth.service.test.ts — it is already compliant (full five-method fake + JWT_SECRET save/restore) and must not be touched.
Any production source change (src/modules/employee/*, src/shared/*, routes, services, repositories) — this is a test-only hardening phase.
Adding new route tests or changing existing assertions/behavior coverage — only the fake's shape changes; the four existing tests and their expectations are preserved.

entityInvariants.invariant: Any object supplied as an IEmployeeService (including test fakes) must implement all five methods — createEmployee, getEmployeeById, getEmployeeByEmail, getEmployeesByManagerId, getEmployeeProfileById — with the exact signatures declared in src/modules/employee/employee.service.interface.ts; a partial object behind a cast is not a valid IEmployeeService.

The profile returned through the GET /employees/me boundary never carries passwordHash or terminationDate; the route test's fake must not alter this contract (the fake returns the existing EmployeeProfile fixture unchanged).

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Called by the route with the actor id resolved from the verified token (request.user), never a client-supplied id; the route test exercises this via the preHandler actor hook.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Throws NotFoundError(404) for an unknown id; the route maps it to { code: 'NOT_FOUND' }.

interfaceConstraints.operation: createEmployee / getEmployeeById / getEmployeeByEmail / getEmployeesByManagerId (unused in this route)
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: In the route-test fake these are throwing stubs; they must never be invoked by the GET /employees/me path, and any invocation must surface as a thrown error rather than a silent undefined.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The fake's five methods must match the IEmployeeService interface exactly (names, parameter lists, return types) as declared in the employee service interface.
The throwing-stub pattern for the four unused methods must mirror the full-fake approach already present in the auth service test (unreachable methods throw an Error naming the method).
The EmployeeProfile fixture and the passwordHash/terminationDate absence assertions must remain consistent with the canonical EmployeeProfile shape (no passwordHash, no terminationDate).

The route-test seam (decorating `employeeService`, `decorateRequest('user', undefined)`, preHandler actor hook, `app.inject`) must stay consistent with the established route-test convention used by the leave route tests.

integrationPoints.why: The test imports IEmployeeService from this entry point; the fake must satisfy the interface as re-exported here.
The route test's actor fixtures use the canonical AuthUser type; the fake change must not disturb the actor-resolution contract.
